overall: The AG found the Wales Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by generally failing to timely approve minutes, declined to audit precise approval dates, and found no violation for not posting minutes online.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve minutes of its 2019 to 2021 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve minutes in a timely manner

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to post its 2019 to 2021 meeting minutes to its website.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to post minutes to a website, but rather to provide meeting minutes upon request within 10 days, if the minutes exist.

allegations.summary: Complaint sought review of precisely when each set of 2019 to 2021 minutes was approved and whether each approval was timely.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review precisely when the Board approved meeting minutes from all three years and whether approval of each set of minutes was timely as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes from 2019 to 2021 within 90 days of receipt of the letter, and certify to the AG's office in writing that it has done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. We further order the Board to create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes from the years 2019 to 2021 within ninety (90) days of the Board’s receipt of this letter, and to certify to our office in writing that it has done so.
